newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Kiwifruit board forecasts small rise in returns.
newsitem.headline: NZ Kiwifruit board forecasts small rise in returns.

text.p: The New Zealand Kiwifruit Marketing Board forecast on Tuesday that average returns per tray would rise to NZ$4.29 from $4.20 in October despite a crop increase of five million trays.
Orchard gate return per hectare was now $15,547 compared with $14,739 last season.

"Forecast export earnings for New Zealand kiwifruit are up a further $5.1 million to $270.8 million with all markets performing strongly as the current season draws to a close," the board said in a statement.
It was the third forecast increase in three months.

Volumes sold to date had surpassed the total sold in 1995 while net revenue had tipped $500 million, outrunning a heavy hit to the bottom line from the appreciation of the New Zealand dollar, the board said.

Europe had turned in a sterling performance, maintaining high volumes and prices deep into the selling season while Japan's performance was far ahead in terms of volumes and revenue compared with recent seasons.
Fruit sold as a percentage of the 62.45 million trays submitted was predicted to be the highest in four years while the 1996 offshore fruit loss was looking to be the lowest in four years.
